_README: THE ONE FILE A COLLEGE FILLS IN.
Copy this to config/institution.json and edit it. Nothing else in the
repository needs to change to deploy for a new institution — not the React
bundle, not a Django setting, not a template.
cp config/institution.example.json config/institution.json
config/institution.json is gitignored, so an upgrade never overwrites your
settings and your settings never end up in a commit.
WHY THIS IS SERVED AT RUNTIME RATHER THAN COMPILED IN
The identity used to live in frontend/src/institute.js, which meant
rebranding required rebuilding a React bundle. A college's IT department
should not need a Node toolchain to change the name on the sign-in page. The
backend reads this file and serves it from /api/institution/; the frontend
fetches it at boot. Changing a value here needs a backend restart, not a
rebuild.
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT HERE
Secrets. Database passwords, the Django SECRET_KEY and the read-only role's
password live in .env, which has different handling and different backup
rules. This file is safe to read, to diff and to attach to a support ticket.
It is served UNAUTHENTICATED, because the sign-in screen has to render
before anyone has signed in — so never put anything sensitive in it.

_comment: 'name' is REQUIRED and ships empty on purpose. First-run setup refuses to
complete until it is set, so no deployment can accidentally go live still
calling itself by a placeholder.

_field_notes.name: Full registered name, as it should appear on the wordmark. Also seeds the generated identity pattern, so a different name gives a genuinely different pattern.
_field_notes.short_name: Used where the full name will not fit — the browser tab, narrow screens. Falls back to 'name' when empty.
_field_notes.descriptor: One factual line under the wordmark. What this system IS, not a slogan; marketing copy on an internal sign-in screen reads as filler.
_field_notes.footnote: Small line at the foot of the identity panel. Set to "" to hide it.
_field_notes.initials: Monogram letters. Derived from 'name' when null, which is right for most names. Override for cases like 'Indian Institute of Technology', where the conventional initials (IIT) are not simply the capitals.
_field_notes.logo_url: Absolute URL or a path under the static root. Left null, the wordmark and monogram stand in — deliberately better than stretching a low-resolution crest.
_field_notes.contact_email: Shown to users when something fails and they need a human. An unreachable address here is worse than none.
_field_notes.contact_url: Optional support or IT helpdesk page.

_comment: Applied at runtime as CSS custom properties on :root.
SCOPE, STATED HONESTLY: these three colours cover the sign-in screen and
the accent used through the application. The full palette in
frontend/tailwind.config.js remains a BUILD-time concern — Tailwind
generates utility classes ahead of time and cannot read a runtime value.
Changing the wider design system still means editing that file and
rebuilding. That is a real limit, not an oversight: making every shade
runtime-settable would mean abandoning Tailwind's static extraction, which
is what keeps the CSS bundle at 29 KB.
Contrast is your responsibility. The shipped values clear WCAG AA against
their backgrounds; a light accent on white will not, and nothing here
checks that for you.
THE COMPLETE LIST OF URLs THIS SYSTEM MAY FETCH. Nothing else is
reachable.
The language model NEVER sees this list and NEVER supplies a URL. It cannot
ask for a page that is not here, because it is not asked which page to get:
selection is done by deterministic keyword matching in web_agent/allowlist.py
against the 'topics' below. An LLM that generated URLs would be an open
proxy with extra steps.
Consequences worth stating:
* The system can never fetch a page nobody put in this file.
* A prompt injection can never cause a fetch, because injected text is
not consulted for URL selection.
* Adding a source is a file edit and a restart — deliberate and
reviewable, which is the point.
FIELDS
id       stable identifier, used in logs
url      the EXACT absolute URL fetched. No wildcards, no patterns.
label    shown to users as the source of the information
topics   lowercase keywords; a question matching these selects this page
enabled  false parks an entry without deleting it
The two entries below are your real pages and ship DISABLED. Enable them
once the URLs are correct. There are deliberately no live sample entries:
a fresh install should not be able to reach the public internet until
someone has decided which pages it may read.
